channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Flávio e Tarcísio cumprem primeira agenda de pré-campanha conjunta na Agrishow, em Ribeirão Preto
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas and presidential pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro held their first joint pre-campaign appearance at Agrishow 2026 in Ribeirão Preto, arriving together and attending the inauguration of a São Paulo government space. The event highlights right-wing coordination amid Jair Bolsonaro's ineligibility, with Flávio leading Lula in a Quaest poll and Tarcísio ahead in Datafolha surveys for the state gubernatorial race.

item.title: Governo Lula ainda busca aceno de Alcolumbre para aprovação 'sem sustos' de Jorge Messias para o STF
item.description: The Lula government is seeking a public gesture from Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to ensure a smooth approval of Jorge Messias for the Supreme Federal Court (STF), with the confirmation hearing scheduled for Wednesday. While the government believes Messias already has 48 votes — above the 41 needed — the lack of explicit support from Alcolumbre poses a risk of last-minute opposition. Minister José Guimarães is working to secure at least a neutral statement from the senator to prevent surprises during the vote.

item.title: Apesar do juro alto, famílias recorrem mais ao rotativo do cartão de crédito; empréstimos somam R$ 110 bi no 1º trimestre
item.description: The use of credit card revolving debt in Brazil reached R$ 109.65 billion in Q1 2024, a 9.7% increase from the same period in 2023, with an annual interest rate of 428.3% in March and a delinquency rate of 63.5%. Around 40 million Brazilians were in revolving credit card debt in January, reflecting the misuse of credit as part of monthly income. The Lula government is pursuing measures to reduce indebtedness, including legal caps limiting total debt to twice the original amount, in the context of the 2026 election year.

item.title: Lula lidera corrida ao Planalto seguido por Flávio, mostra BTG/Nexus
item.description: Lula leads the 2026 presidential race with 41% of voting intentions, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 36%, according to the BTG/Nexus poll. Romeu Zema and Ronaldo Caiado trail with 4% and 3%. In a potential runoff, the two frontrunners are technically tied, within the poll's 2-point margin of error.

item.title: Semana tem sabatina de Messias e análise do veto de Lula ao PL da Dosimetria
item.description: The week of April 27-30, 2026 in the Brazilian National Congress focuses on the sabatina of Jorge Messias, Lula’s nominee for the STF, taking place Wednesday in the CCJ and requiring 41 favorable votes in the plenary for approval. On Thursday, deputies and senators will convene in a joint session to analyze Lula’s veto of the Dosimetria Bill, which reduces penalties for those convicted of the January 8 attacks and was seen as an attempt to benefit Jair Bolsonaro. To overturn the veto, an absolute majority is required: 257 deputies and 41 senators, with separate voting.

item.title: Congresso pode restabelecer PL da Dosimetria nesta semana
item.description: Congress is set to review on Thursday President Lula's full veto of the Dosimetria bill, which reduces sentences for those involved in the January 8 coup attempt, including former President Jair Bolsonaro. The expectation is that the veto will be overturned, reinstating the sentence reductions, as government allies believe Lula's decision is unlikely to stand. A potential agreement with the Centrão bloc was undermined by fears that maintaining the veto would trigger an opposition push for a parliamentary inquiry into Banco Master, a move many lawmakers oppose.

item.title: Carlos Bolsonaro cutuca Zema e diz que Flávio ‘está mordendo a isca’
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro (PL-SC) criticized former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo-MG) for supporting the tax reform, arguing it raises taxes and worries investors in Santa Catarina and across Brazil. He also accused right-wing allies of attempting to politically bury Jair Bolsonaro and urged Flávio Bolsonaro to stop 'biting the bait' of false alliances, calling for unity on the right to win in the first round of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Governo tenta frear pautas-bomba com impacto bilionário em ano eleitoral; veja quais são
item.description: The federal government is mobilizing its economic team, the Civil House, and the Secretariat of Institutional Relations to block at least seven high-impact electoral proposals in Congress that could cost billions, including minimum wage floors for health and education professionals, expanded pension benefits, and revenue earmarking. The main concern is the PEC do Suas, which mandates a 1% allocation of Net Current Revenue to the Unified Social Assistance System (SUAS), already approved in the first round in the Chamber and under negotiation in the Senate. The effort aims to safeguard the fiscal framework and uphold credibility in economic policy during an election year.

item.title: Voo da Gol do Galeão para NY, anunciado em evento com Lula, estará disponível só de julho a outubro
item.description: Gol announced a direct flight from Rio de Janeiro’s Galeão Airport to New York in March during an event with Lula, with service set to begin in July. Although ticket sales started as promised, data submitted to Anac show the route will operate only 46 flights through October 21, indicating a short duration. The Rio de Janeiro City Hall provided a R$6 million incentive to enable the new route.

item.title: Frase do dia
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema, a pre-candidate for president of Brazil, stated in an interview with Metrópoles that he plans to privatize Petrobras and Banco do Brasil, and cut excessive salaries, privileges, and schemes that sustain Brazil’s untouchable elite in Brasília. The remarks underscore his liberal agenda and commitment to ending public-sector privileges.

item.title: Figueiredo dá “spoiler” sobre chance de Trump declarar apoio a Flávio
item.description: Bolsonarist influencer Paulo Figueiredo, a close ally of Eduardo Bolsonaro in the U.S., stated that Donald Trump will not publicly endorse Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 Brazilian elections. According to Figueiredo, Flávio has made clear he does not seek U.S. presidential backing, but rather diplomatic pressure for free and transparent elections in the U.S. The article also notes that PT leaders hope for such a Trump endorsement to use it as evidence that Flávio would 'deliver Brazil' to the U.S., reinforcing their sovereignty narrative.

item.title: “Já gastaram mais de meio milhão”, diz Flávio sobre mentiras do PT nas redes
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, claimed opponents have spent over R$500,000 on disinformation campaigns against him on social media. He said he has taken legal action in response to what he described as false accusations from the PT. The statement was made in a video posted on Sunday, the 26th, on his social media accounts.

item.title: Tarcísio e Flávio “abrem” pré-campanha em SP na Agrishow
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and Governor Tarcísio de Freitas jointly opened the Agrishow in Ribeirão Preto, marking their first public appearance together after defining their pre-candidacies. The event, Latin America’s largest agribusiness fair, serves as a platform for Tarcísio, coordinator of Flávio’s pre-campaign in São Paulo, to reduce productive sector resistance to the senator. Other presidential pre-candidates, including Romeu Zema and Ronaldo Caiado, are expected to attend, while Lula did not participate.

item.title: A popularidade de Lula a quase 5 meses da eleição, segundo pesquisa Nexus
item.description: Lula’s government is rated as good or excellent by 33% of voters, bad or terrible by 43%, and regular by 23%, according to a Nexus poll from April 2026. Approval of the government rose from 45% to 46%, while disapproval fell from 51% to 49%, with 5% undecided. The survey interviewed 2,028 voters by phone between April 24 and 26, with a two-point margin of error.

item.title: Desafio do Parque Bruno Covas vai além de capivaras e segurança
item.description: The São Paulo government has published a bid for a 48-month concession of Bruno Covas Linear Park, aiming to improve security and infrastructure through access control, surveillance cameras, and integration with the Muralha Paulista and Smart Sampa systems. Although short-term contracts are uncommon in the sector, the government reports interest from companies and remains optimistic that the concession will address user concerns while keeping access free and protecting local wildlife, including capybaras.

item.title: As intenções de voto de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro no 2º turno, em nova pesquisa Nexus
item.description: A Nexus poll released on April 27, 2026 shows a technical tie between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in a potential 2026 presidential runoff, with Lula numerically ahead at 46% to 45%. The margin of error is two percentage points, and the combined share of blank/null/no response increased to 9%. Alternative scenarios with Romeu Zema and Ronaldo Caiado also show Lula leading, albeit by a smaller margin.

item.title: Frentes querem transformar escala 6 X 1 em nova reforma trabalhista
item.description: Parliamentary fronts, led by the FPE, aim to reframe the debate on ending the 6X1 work schedule as a broader labor reform, seeking to constitutionally entrench elements of the Temer-era reform, such as prioritizing negotiated agreements over legislation, limiting Labor Ministry regulations, and restricting judicial labor rulemaking. The strategy is to delay approval of the reduced workweek until the 2026 elections, pressuring the Lula government to disclose fiscal impacts and funding sources, while avoiding direct opposition from pre-candidates due to electoral concerns.

item.title: Ala do STF vê acórdão do TSE como 'insuficiente' para sanar dúvidas, e julgamento sobre eleição no Rio deve ter novo desgaste entre Cortes
item.description: STF ministers consider the TSE's ruling insufficient to determine whether the vacancy in Rio's governorship is electoral in nature, reigniting tensions between the courts. The ruling lacks a clear stance on the cassation of Cláudio Castro's diploma and the effects of his resignation, leaving the STF awaiting Justice Flávio Dino's vote-vista. The outcome will decide whether the governorship is filled by direct popular election or indirect appointment by the state legislature, with a deadline in December.

item.title: Indicação de Messias ao STF passará pela CCJ do Senado com favoritismo ao indicado por Lula
item.description: The Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) will hear Attorney General Jorge Messias on Wednesday, Lula's nominee to fill the STF vacancy left by Luís Roberto Barroso. Despite opposition opposition, approval in the CCJ and full Senate is expected, with Messias gaining support even from some Bolsonarist senators after a targeted outreach campaign. Rapporteur Weverton Rocha praised Messias's professional and academic background and said the full Senate vote could follow the same day.

item.title: Agenda da semana: sabatina de Messias e análise do PL da Dosimetria
item.description: This week’s political agenda features the Senate hearing of Jorge Messias for the STF, the TSE trial that may remove Roraima’s governor Edilson Damião, and the congressional review of Lula’s veto on a bill reducing penalties for the January 8 events. Additional highlights include debates on the diesel import subsidy via MP 1.349/2026 and coordinated interest rate decisions between Brazil and the U.S.

item.title: Messias entra em semana decisiva ainda contando votos para o STF
item.description: AGU Minister Jorge Messias is in a decisive phase for his Supreme Court nomination, with 13 declared votes in his favor in the Senate's CCJ committee and needing just one more for majority approval. Of the 27 committee members, five remain undeclared, with two (Cid Gomes and Rodrigo Pacheco) seen as government allies likely to support him, while Oriovisto Guimarães is expected to vote against. If approved in the CCJ, Messias believes he has 45 guaranteed votes in the full Senate — above the 41 needed — with the Planalto aiming for 50 to ensure a smoother process.

item.title: Jardim supera melhor sequência de vitórias de Filipe Luís no Flamengo e se aproxima de marca de Jorge Jesus
item.description: Leonardo Jardim achieved his seventh consecutive victory with Flamengo, surpassing Filipe Luís's best streak and approaching Jorge Jesus's record of ten straight wins. The Portuguese coach has secured an 82% point return across 13 matches, showing consistent performance in the Brasileirão, Libertadores, and Copa do Brasil. Jardim emphasized that his focus is on the team's collective performance, not individual accolades.

item.title: Alckmin anuncia R$ 10 bilhões para a modernização de máquinas agrícolas
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin announced a new R$ 10 billion credit line for agricultural machinery modernization under the MOVE Brasil program during the Agrishow opening in Ribeirão Preto. The funds, sourced from the surplus of the National Fund for Scientific and Technological Development (Finep), will be available in 20 to 30 days through cooperatives, private banks, and Banco do Brasil, with low interest rates. Alckmin also previewed a rural debt renegotiation program for both current and delinquent producers to boost sector competitiveness.

item.title: A escolta de 44 policiais do ex-governador Cláudio Castro
item.description: The TSE upheld the conviction of former governor Cláudio Castro for abuse of economic power, but did not remove his post-office benefits, as he was not cassated. The ruling allows him to retain institutional privileges tied to his former governorship.

item.title: Moraes concede prisão domiciliar a ‘Fátima de Tubarão’, condenada pelo 8 de Janeiro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes granted house arrest to Maria de Fátima Souza, known as 'Fátima de Tubarão', who was sentenced to 17 years in prison for her role in the January 8, 2023, coup attempt. She has already served three years, ten months, and 24 days of her sentence and must wear an electronic ankle monitor, with bans on social media use, leaving Brazil, and contacting other participants. Moraes warned that violating these conditions would lead to revocation of house arrest and return to prison.

item.title: PT estimula Kassab a patrocinar candidato de centro em SP; entenda
item.description: PT leaders are urging Gilberto Kassab, president of the PSD, to sponsor a centrist candidate for the São Paulo gubernatorial race in 2026, aiming to force a runoff and prevent Tarcísio de Freitas from winning in the first round. Although Kassab has publicly backed Tarcísio, Haddad’s allies believe he may be resentful over being sidelined in the governor’s re-election slate, particularly after Felício Ramuth left the PSD for the MDB and Rodrigo Garcia, a Kassab rival, was brought into Tarcísio’s campaign.

item.title: A pergunta da semana que está na boca de todo mundo
item.description: The nomination of Jorge Messias, Attorney General of the Union, to the Supreme Federal Court hinges on Senate approval, with David Alcolumbre maintaining opposition despite no longer having an alternative candidate. The confirmation hearing will take place the day after tomorrow (Wednesday, 20), while STF ministers like Flávio Dino work against the nomination and Kassio Nunes Marques and André Mendonça support it. The uncertainty carries significant political weight, as the outcome will influence the ideological balance of the Court.

item.title: Lula fica fora da Agrishow e amplia o terreno da oposição com o agronegócio
item.description: Lula did not attend Agrishow 2026, expanding opposition space in agribusiness during an election year. Flávio Bolsonaro, Ronaldo Caiado, and Romeu Zema confirmed attendance, using the event to criticize the government. The fair has become a political barometer, with a history of tensions between the agribusiness sector and Lula’s government since 2023.

item.title: Novas regras, parcerias regionais e classe média: como Lula reforça Minha Casa, Minha Vida em sua vitrine eleitoral
item.description: The Lula government is strengthening the Minha Casa, Minha Vida program as a central pillar of its 2026 electoral strategy, highlighting robust results in home ownership access despite high household indebtedness. The initiative aims to consolidate support among the middle class and low-income families through new rules and regional partnerships, turning the program into a showcase of achievements from his third term.

item.title: Missão arrecadar: a estratégia do governo para alcançar o superávit das contas a partir de 2027
item.description: The government aims to sustain its revenue-raising efforts starting in 2027, should President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva be re-elected, focusing on reducing tax exemptions ('tax expenditures') and increasing the progressivity of the tax system—meaning higher contributions from the wealthy. The strategy seeks to achieve a fiscal surplus from that year onward, despite previous measures already implemented. The article is exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: Geopolítica e economia verde marcam presença do Brasil na feira industrial Hannover Messe 2026, na Alemanha
item.description: Brazil stood out at Hannover Messe 2026 with 800 business representatives from 300 companies, reinforcing its image as a stable and open partner in the global energy transition, particularly in biofuels and strategic minerals. President Lula’s meeting with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz underscored political alignment as a commercial advantage, even as he criticized EU regulations that could hinder Brazilian biofuel exports.

item.title: Em meio a pressão de Carlos, governadores bolsonaristas demonstram pouco engajamento nas redes à pré-campanha de Flávio
item.description: Bolsonarist governors have shown low engagement on social media in support of Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-candidacy, despite public pressure from his brother Carlos Bolsonaro for greater mobilization. Only Santa Catarina's governor, Jorginho Mello, has made explicit posts in Flávio's favor, though limited to three since January. Others, including Tarcísio de Freitas, Celina Leão, Ibaneis Rocha, and Wilson Lima, have made minimal or no mentions of Flávio on their official accounts.

item.title: Apoios a Lula e caso Master: entenda por que o PT suavizou tom de manifesto aprovado durante congresso nacional
item.description: The PT approved a manifesto during its national congress in Brasília, aiming to strengthen support for the re-election of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The document proposes judicial and political reforms, including changes to parliamentary amendments, and seeks dialogue with centrist parties through a 'social concertation'.

item.title: 59% dos brasileiros dizem que renda é insuficiente
item.description: A Datafolha survey from April 2026 shows that 59% of Brazilians say their household income is insufficient to cover expenses, 36% say it is exactly what they need, and 6% say it is more than enough. The survey also found that 45% sought to supplement their income recently, with higher rates among the more educated, and that 4 in 10 respondents reported a reduction in family income over the past months, particularly among those aged 35 to 44.

item.title: Dosimetria volta ao Congresso nesta semana com iminente derrota do Planalto
item.description: Brazil's National Congress will convene in its first joint session of 2026 this Thursday (April 30) to decide whether to override President Lula's veto on the dosimetry bill, which seeks to reduce sentences for those convicted in the January 8 attacks. Approved in late 2025 during a low point in Lula-Legislature relations, the bill could reduce former President Jair Bolsonaro's 27-year-and-3-month sentence for leading a coup plot after the 2022 election to approximately two years in closed regime. The opposition, holding a majority in the Chamber, aims to overturn the veto with over 300 votes, while Lula's allies anticipate defeat amid mounting political pressure ahead of the 2026 general elections.

item.title: Veja medidas do pacote contra endividamento previsto para 1º de maio
item.description: The Lula government is preparing a package of measures to reduce household debt in Brazil, with an announcement expected on May 1st. The plan includes reformulating the Desenrola Brasil program with broader discounts on bank and non-bank debts, using public guarantees via the FGO to lower interest rates, and analyzing the use of FGTS funds to help workers pay off high-cost debts.

item.title: Em busca de bandeira para Lula na segurança, governo mira em integração com estados em nova fase de programa de combate a roubo de celular
item.description: The Lula government is preparing a new phase of the national program to combat cellphone theft, focusing on integrating data from police reports, IMEIs, and state security systems, inspired by Piauí’s experience. The initiative aims to improve identification, blocking, and return of stolen devices, including notifications for buyers of stolen phones, as part of a strategy to boost the president’s popularity amid high public concern over this crime.

item.title: Desafio do lulismo é oferecer não só inclusão, mas também perspectiva
item.description: The recent decline in Lula’s popularity reflects a deeper disconnect between the inclusive social rhetoric of lulism and a society marked by precarity, debt, and new aspirations. The article argues that the challenge for the government goes beyond communication or economic performance, requiring a new vision that engages with Brazil’s structural transformations.

item.title: Motta escolhe nesta semana relator da PEC do fim da escala 6x1
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB) will choose this week the rapporteur for the PEC proposing the end of the 6x1 work scale, following negotiations among party leaders. Deputy Paulo Azi (União Brasil-BA), who served as rapporteur in the Constitution and Justice Committee, is a leading candidate, while Solidarity Party leader Paulinho da Força was also mentioned. The appointment will coincide with the installation of a special committee to analyze the proposal, which aims to reduce the weekly workweek to 40 hours or adopt a 5x2 scale — a key electoral issue for President Lula’s government.

item.title: Zema sugere que Gilmar parece personagem de “A Praça é Nossa”
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) shared on his X profile a clip from an interview on Rádio Cultura de Catalão where, upon hearing Minister Gilmar Mendes, he compared him to Deputy João Plenário from the comedy show 'A Praça é Nossa'. The comment referenced the minister's speech being hard to understand, a point Zema had previously addressed in his AI-generated series 'Os Intocáveis'. Zema and Mendes have exchanged public criticisms in recent weeks, including over speech style and use of private jets.

item.title: Bolsonaro cumpre pena em casa com piscina e de tornozeleira; veja infográfico
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro, sentenced to 27 years and three months for attempted coup, is serving house arrest in a luxury home with a pool and garden in Solar de Brasília, having left the Papudinha prison cell. The infographic highlights the contrast between his former incarceration and current residence in Brasília’s upscale Jardim Botânico neighborhood.

item.title: Bolsonaro completa um mês em casa com filmes, cachorros e Michelle confinada em rotina de cuidados
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro completes one month of house arrest at his Brasília residence, spending time watching TV and moderately interacting with his dogs. Former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro oversees his care, having withdrawn from public and political life.

item.title: PT produz vídeo para tentar vincular Flávio Bolsonaro ao caso Master
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) released a video attempting to link Flávio Bolsonaro to the Master Bank scandal, claiming he received a R$6 million mansion as part of a so-called 'bolsomaster' scheme. However, Bolsonaro is not under investigation in the case, and the mansion was purchased in 2021 via BRB financing, prior to the bank’s 2024–2025 involvement with Master. The video was circulated during the PT’s 8th National Congress in Brasília, reflecting a mutual blame game between PT and Bolsonaro supporters over the scandal’s origins.

item.title: Fernando Schüler estreia série de encontros sobre futuro do Brasil no Teatro Iguatemi
item.description: Political scientist Fernando Schüler launches the 'Contemporary Brazil' series of talks at Teatro Iguatemi, with the first debate scheduled for April 27 at 8 PM, featuring former state deputy Heni Ozi Cukier. The initiative aims to analyze the challenges and prospects of contemporary Brazil.

item.title: Erika Hilton acusa Tarcísio de favorecer bolsonaristas em ato na Paulista
item.description: Deputy Erika Hilton (Psol-SP) accused Governor Tarcísio de Freitas of attempting to prevent workers from holding a demonstration on Paulista Avenue on May 1st, Labor Day, to demand the end of the 6×1 work schedule. She claimed the governor was favoring Bolsonaristas by restricting the right to strike and protest.

item.title: Violência política de esquerda cresceu na era Trump e deixa uma lição para o Brasil
item.description: The content analyzes the rise of left-wing political violence in the U.S. during the Trump era, citing CSIS data showing that, in the first half of 2025, leftist attacks surpassed right-wing ones for the first time, though they are generally less lethal. Despite Trump avoiding labeling the recent shooter as 'radical left,' the pattern of hostility toward him persists. The text offers a lesson for Brazil about the dangers of polarization and the legitimization of political violence, regardless of ideological spectrum.

item.title: PT aprova manifesto sem citar escândalo do Banco Master
item.description: The Workers' Party approved its 2026 electoral manifesto following adjustments requested by the Presidential Palace. The final version removed direct references to former President Jair Bolsonaro and the Banco Master scandal, softening the original criticism. The document retains the party's political guidelines for the election year, emphasizing unity and campaign strategy.

item.title: Moraes concede prisão domiciliar a 18 idosos do 8 de Janeiro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes granted humanitarian house arrest to 18 elderly individuals convicted for the January 8 attacks, all aged between 60 and 73 and suffering from serious illnesses. The ruling comes six days before Congress votes on the presidential veto of the Dosimetry Bill and includes electronic ankle monitoring, bans on social media, international travel, and unauthorized visits.

item.title: PT lança diretrizes que governo do PT não foi capaz de entregar
item.description: The PT approved three documents at its Congress: a manifesto aimed at softening an electoral tactic and the guidelines for a potential fourth Lula term. The texts reveal plans that the current PT government failed to deliver, highlighting a gap between party proposals and governmental achievements. This suggests the party is attempting to reposition itself amid criticism over poor implementation.

item.title: PT fala em ser “antissistema” e quer colar Bolsonaro à velha política
item.description: At its 8th National Congress in April 2026, the PT reclaimed the 'anti-system' discourse to reposition itself as an alternative to the current political model, advocating for electoral, judicial, and economic reforms while criticizing the PL and fascism as representatives of the old politics. PT president Edinho Silva stated that the response to public outrage for change lies on the left and that the Lula government embodies this anti-system stance, seeking to distance the party from recent scandals such as the Banco Master case.
